source_text: Οὐ γὰρ τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ ζητούμενον μόνον, ἵνα ἀναστῶμεν καὶ ἐνδυσώμεθα ἀθανασίαν, ἀλλ' ἵνα ἀναστάντες καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὴν ἀθανασίαν, μὴ γυμνοὶ δόξης εὑρεθῶμεν, καὶ τῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν παῤῥησίας· ἵνα μὴ τῷ πυρὶ παραδοθῶμεν. Διὰ τοῦτό φησιν· Εἴ γε καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι, οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα. Εἶτα πάλιν ἀξιοπιστότερον ποιῶν τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγον, εἰπὼν, ὅτι μέλλει καταπίνεσθαι τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς, ἐπήγαγεν· Ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο Θεός. Ὃ δὲ λέγει τοῦτό ἐστιν· Ἐξ ἀρχῆς διὰ τοῦτο τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἔπλασεν, οὐχ ἵνα ἀπόληται, ἀλλ' ἵνα πρὸς ἀφθαρσίαν ὁδεύῃ. Ὥστε καὶ ἡνίκα τὸν θάνατον συνεχώρησε, μετὰ τοιαύτης αὐτὸν συνεχώρησε γνώμης, ἵνα σωφρονισθῇς ἀπὸ τῆς κολάσεως, καὶ βελτίων γενόμενος, δυνηθῇς πρὸς τὴν ἀθανασίαν ἀχθῆναι πάλιν. Καὶ ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ ἀρχῆς αὕτη παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐκράτει ἡ βουλὴ καὶ ἡ γνώμη, καὶ μετὰ ταύτης τῆς ψήφου τὸν πρῶτον διέπλασεν ἄνθρωπον· τοῦτο εὐθέως καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἡμῖν ᾐνίξατο τῶν προοιμίων. Εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἐβούλετο τὰς θύρας ἡμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἀνοῖξαι, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκε τὸν Ἄβελ πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν ἐπιδειξάμενον, καὶ φίλον αὐτῷ γεγενημένον, παθεῖν ἅπερ ἔπαθε. Νυνὶ δὲ ἡμῖν ἐνδεικνύμενος, ὅτι πρὸς ἑτέραν ζωὴν ὁδεύομεν, καί τις αἰὼν ἕτερος ὑπολέλειπται τῶν δικαίων, ἔχων τὰς ἀμοιβὰς καὶ τοὺς στεφάνους ἀποκειμένους, τὸν πρῶτον γενόμενον δίκαιον μὴ λαβόντα ἐνταῦθα τοὺς μισθοὺς, ὧν ἐπόνεσεν, ἀφῆκεν ἀπελθεῖν βοῶντα, δι' ὧν ἔπαθε, πᾶσι καὶ λέγοντα, ὅτι μετὰ τὴν ἐντεῦθεν ζωὴν ἔστιν ἀνταπόδοσίς τις καὶ μισθὸς καὶ ἀμοιβή. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τὸν Ἐνὼχ μετέθηκε, καὶ τὸν Ἠλίαν ἀνήρπασεν, αἰνιττόμενος ἡμῖν τὸ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως δόγμα. Ἀρκεῖ μὲν οὖν εἰς πληροφορίαν ἡ τοῦ ποιοῦντος δύναμις· εἰ δὲ ἀσθενέστερός τίς ἐστι, καὶ βούλεται ἀπόδειξιν ἑτέραν λαβεῖν καὶ ἐνέχυρον τῆς μελλούσης ἀναστάσεως, καὶ τοῦτο μετὰ πολλῆς τῆς δαψιλείας ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς, τὴν τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριν μετὰ πολλῆς ἐπαφεὶς τῆς ἀφθονίας. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ Παῦλος ποιήσας ἀξιόπιστον τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγον ἀπὸ τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀναστάσεως, ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεὸν εἶναι τὸν δημιουργοῦντα, ἐπάγει καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ῥητὸν, λέγων, ὅτι καὶ ἀῤῥαβῶνα ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν, οὐ χρημάτων οὐδὲ χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου, ἀλλ' ἀῤῥαβῶνα Πνεύματος· ὁ δὲ ἀῤῥαβὼν μέρος ἐστὶ τοῦ παντὸς, καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ παντὸς πιστός. Καθάπερ γὰρ ἐπὶ τῶν συμβολαίων ὁ τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα δεξάμενος ὑπὲρ τοῦ παντὸς θαῤῥεῖ λοιπὸν καὶ πεπίστευκεν, οὕτω καὶ σὺ λαβὼν ἀῤῥαβῶνα, τοῦ Πνεύματος τὰ χαρίσματα λέγω, μηκέτι ἀμφίβαλε περὶ τῶν ἀποκειμένων ἀγαθῶν. Ὁ γὰρ νεκροὺς ἀνιστὰς, ὁ τυφλοὺς θεραπεύων, ὁ δαίμονας ἀπελαύνων, ὁ λεπροὺς καθαίρων, ὁ νοσήματα διορθούμενος, ὁ θάνατον λύων, ὁ τοσαῦτα καὶ τηλικαῦτα δυνάμενος ἐν ἐπικήρῳ καὶ θνητῷ σώματι, ποίας τεύξῃ συγγνώμης ἀμφιβάλλων περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως; Εἰ γὰρ μηδέπω τοῦ καιροῦ τῆς ἀντιδόσεως παραγενομένου, ἀλλ' ἔτι τῶν παλαισμάτων ἑστώτων, τοσούτοις ἡμᾶς ἠμείψατο στεφάνοις ὁ Θεὸς, ἐννόησον ὅσα σοι κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τὸν τῶν βραβείων δώσει τὰ ἀγαθά. Εἰ δὲ λέγοι τις· Ἀλλ' οὐχ ὁρῶμεν ταῦτα νῦν γινόμενα τὰ σημεῖα, οὐδὲ ἡμεῖς τοσαύτην ἔχομεν δύναμιν· ἐκεῖνο ἂν εἴποιμι, ὅτι οὐδὲν διαφέρει, εἴτε νῦν, εἴτε πρότερον ταῦτα γεγένηται.
thought_title: The resurrection as God's original purpose, shown by Abel, Enoch, Elijah, and the Spirit's guarantee
orientation: Chrysostom continues expounding 2 Corinthians 5:3-5, explaining that God created humanity for incorruption and gave signs and the Spirit as a guarantee of the coming resurrection.

choices.why: ψῆφος here means God's sovereign resolve or decree, not a ballot or vote; 'decree' preserves the sense of a fixed divine purpose.
The glossary requires 'guarantee' for ἀρραβών, the Spirit as a down payment or pledge of future goods.
The glossary requires 'confidence' for παῤῥησία, boldness before God.
The glossary requires 'incorruption' for ἀφθαρσία, the state of the risen body.
ἀθανασία is distinct from ἀφθαρσία in this passage; 'immortality' preserves the distinction from 'incorruption' used for ἀφθαρσία.
παλαίσματα refers to wrestling contests, fitting the athletic contest imagery of the homily; 'wrestling matches' keeps the concrete athletic sense.

pass_b_english: For the question is not only that we rise and put on immortality, but that after rising and putting on immortality, we may not be found naked of glory and of confidence before God—so that we may not be handed over to the fire. That is why he says: “If indeed, having put it on, we will not be found naked” (2 Corinthians 5:3). Then, making the argument about the resurrection more trustworthy, after saying that what is mortal is going to be swallowed up by life, he added: “And the one who worked us for this very thing is God” (2 Corinthians 5:5). What he means is this: from the beginning God formed the human being for this purpose, not so that he might perish, but so that he might journey toward incorruption. So even when he permitted death, he permitted it with this intention: that you might be disciplined by the punishment, and having become better, you might be able to be led again to immortality. From above and from the beginning this counsel and purpose prevailed with God, and with this decree he formed the first human being. He hinted this to us immediately from the very opening events. For if he had not wanted to open the doors of the resurrection to us from the beginning, he would not have allowed Abel, who had displayed every virtue and had become his friend, to suffer what he suffered. But now, showing us that we are journeying toward another life, and that another age remains for the righteous, holding the rewards and crowns laid up, he allowed the first righteous man, who did not receive here the wages of his labors, to depart crying out through what he suffered, saying to all that after this life there is a recompense and a wage and a reward. For this reason he also translated Enoch and snatched up Elijah, hinting to us the doctrine of the resurrection. The power of the Maker is enough for full assurance. But if someone is weaker and wants to receive another proof and a pledge of the coming resurrection, God gave this too with great abundance, pouring out the grace of the Spirit with great generosity. For this reason Paul, after making the argument about the resurrection trustworthy from the resurrection of Christ and from God being the Creator, adds this saying as well, saying that he also gave us a guarantee—not of money, nor of gold and silver, but a guarantee of the Spirit. And a guarantee is a part of the whole, and it is trustworthy for the whole. For just as in contracts the one who has received the guarantee is confident about the whole from then on and has believed, so you too, having received the guarantee—I mean the gifts of the Spirit—no longer doubt about the good things laid up for you. For the one who raises the dead, who heals the blind, who drives out demons, who cleanses lepers, who sets diseases right, who looses death, who can do such great things in a perishable and mortal body—what pardon will you obtain if you doubt about the resurrection? For if the time of recompense has not yet come, but the wrestling matches are still standing, and God has already rewarded us with so many crowns, consider how many good things he will give you at the time of the prizes. But if someone says: “We do not see these signs happening now, and we do not have such power,” I would say this: it makes no difference whether these things happened now or before.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριν μετὰ πολλῆς ἐπαφεὶς τῆς ἀφθονίας
last_rejected.why: ἐπαφεὶς means 'adding/bestowing upon', not 'pouring out'; the sense is God added the Spirit's grace upon the abundance already given.
last_rejected.fix: adding the grace of the Spirit with great abundance
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπαφεὶς from ἐπιχέω means 'pour upon'; 'pouring out' is accurate, not 'adding upon abundance'.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ γὰρ νεκροὺς ἀνιστὰς, ὁ τυφλοὺς θεραπεύων, ὁ δαίμονας ἀπελαύνων, ὁ λεπροὺς καθαίρων, ὁ νοσήματα διορθούμενος, ὁ θάνατον λύων
last_rejected.why: English presents as God's acts, but Greek uses articular participles without explicit subject, continuing from Spirit's gifts; likely refers to Christ or Spirit's power through believers, not directly God's acts.
last_rejected.fix: For the one raising the dead, healing the blind, driving out demons...
last_rejected.ruling: Articular participles continue the subject from context; no meaning is changed or lost by leaving it implicit.

last_rejected.why: "Looses death" is nonsensical; λύω here means destroys/undoes death, i.e., raises dead or overcomes death.
last_rejected.fix: who undoes death, or who breaks the power of death
last_rejected.ruling: λύω can mean 'loose/dissolve'; 'looses death' is unusual but within the word's range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the wrestling matches are still standing
last_rejected.why: "Standing" for ἑστώτων misses idiom; means contests are still ongoing/in progress, not static.
last_rejected.fix: while the contests are still going on
last_rejected.ruling: ἑστώτων 'standing' for ongoing contests is a valid literal rendering; 'still standing' conveys ongoing, not static.
